pairs.why: Both are bright mid-key scenes with a light-grey hero on mid-green grass and soft shadows, so value gives no clear reason to choose.
B's hero is a darker, mid-value green with a calmer, darker background, close to the real card. A's lime pockets and bright glow behind the pack push it brighter and harder than the real card.
A's light, gently graded striped background and soft shadow around the clock match the real card's key, while B's darker, more saturated stripes and hard ground shadow don't.
A's asteroid is a mid-value body with gentle crater shading. B has large near-dark holes and a heavier dark mass, which gives harder local contrast than the real cards' smooth mid-value heroes.
Both have a light hero on mid-green grass with similar soft shadows and bright sky. Neither has the real card's deep tree and ground shadows.
A's pump and sky stay softer and closer in key to the real card. B's darker base and slot details, plus the bright sun glow, add accents the real card doesn't have.
A's hat is a soft purple-dark mass with gentle local contrast. B's near-black hat with a hard white highlight is harsher than the real heroes' saturated navy.
B's navy-grey engine is lighter and broken up by small red and light details, so it has a smaller darkest area. A's large near-black block is darker than the real cards' dark accents.
